welcome.text: The new sign on the fence has been noted. I have opened a clean page in my big book.
I saw the new sign on the fence. It has the crisp look of a letter worth keeping.
New sign up. It stays bright against the wet cobbles.
The new sign means a clear morning. A warm cup follows.

quiet.text: The upper hall window was lit after sunset. I entered it in the margin, where proper occurrences go.
I weighed three parcels before noon. One was lighter than its string.
Hard rain last night. The cobbles are nearly black, and one leaf has settled on the fountain lip again.
The queue reaches the fountain today. The last cup in line stays warm.

first.text: Your post has left the road out of town. I filed it in my big book. Proper correspondence begins somewhere.
I weighed your post as it passed the scale. It had the useful weight of a parcel with no parcel.
On my sweeping round, I saw your post leave the road out of town. The square keeps such things moving.
Over the counter, I heard your post had gone out. The cups are expecting a little more traffic.

cabin.text: A cabin now stands on the road out of town. I filed the cabin in my big book. The entry sits properly.
That cabin on the road out of town looks sound. I judged it against the scale. It outweighs a tent.
Past the orchard, I saw the cabin on my sweeping round. It has settled onto the road out of town.
From the counter, I heard about the cabin on the road out of town. Cups travel faster than feet.

house.text: A house now stands on the road out of town. I filed the house in my big book. Properly entered.
The house on the road out of town has some weight to it. The scale would approve, if it could see.
Along the road out of town, I saw the house on my sweeping round. It holds the edge of town nicely.
At the counter, I heard the house is on the road out of town. A cup says the road looks fuller.

fixed.text: The square is in order again. I filed the change in my big book. The fountain has fewer complaints.
The square looks lighter on the scale today. You set it right. Noted.
On my sweeping round, the square looked put right. The cobbles show it plainly.
Over the counter, I heard you put the square right. The queue has stopped looking at the bin.

curse.text: Last night left the square in a poor state. I filed the night in my big book. The lamps have resumed their duties.
The night left the square looking like a parcel dropped in a puddle. I checked it against the scale. Uneven.
After the night, I swept the square on my round. The ghosts left litter where leaves usually gather.
From the counter, I heard about the night in the square. The cups are rattling less now.
